import re
import pytest
from target import url_basename

# Reference implementation using the old regex
def _old_url_basename(url: str) -> str:
    m = re.match(r'(?:https?:|)//[^/]+/(?:[^?#]+/)?([^/?#]+)/?(?:[?#]|$)', url)
    return m.group(1) if m else u''

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url",
    [
        # Simple cases
        "http://example.com/foo",
        "https://example.com/foo/",
        "http://example.com/foo?bar=baz",
        "https://example.com/foo#section",
        "http://example.com/foo/?query=1",
        "https://example.com/foo/#frag",
        # Trailing slash without basename
        "http://example.com/",
        "https://example.com",
        # Multiple path components (old regex should capture the last one)
        "http://example.com/a/b/c",
        "https://example.com/one/two/three/",
        "http://example.com/x/y/z?param=val",
        "https://example.com/p/q/r#anchor",
        # URLs with port numbers
        "http://example.com:8080/foo",
        "https://example.com:443/bar/baz",
        # URLs with user info
        "http://user:pass@example.com/foo",
        "https://user@example.com/a/b",
        # IPv4 and IPv6 hosts
        "http://127.0.0.1/foo",
        "https://[2001:db8::1]/bar",
        # Encoded characters
        "http://example.com/%E6%BC%A2%E5%AD%97",
        "https://example.com/%20space%20/",
        # Query/fragment only (no basename)
        "http://example.com/?q=1",
        "https://example.com/#top",
        # Edge cases with unusual but valid characters
        "http://example.com/!$&'()*+,;=:@",
        "https://example.com/äöüß",
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_matches_old_behavior(url):
    assert url_basename(url) == _old_url_basename(url)
